claim: Coverage, coherence (consistency, plausibility, completeness) and uniqueness are stated as verbal principles with no weights or formula; uniqueness changes confidence, not which story is accepted.
agent_test: Implement coverage = share of evidence items explained, coherence = contradiction count, uniqueness = gap to runner-up; compare to plain pick at equal tokens.

claim: Pennington and Hastie give no theory of what makes a good story and no combining rule, so any scoring formula is our own design, not a validated one.
agent_test: Ablate each principle separately and in combination; report which weights matter.

claim: Coherence shift: after reading an ambiguous case, ratings of disputed arguments move to agree with the leaning verdict (Holyoak and Simon 1999 Exp1 F(1,44)=35.3, N=48; Simon 2001 Exp1 F(2,86)=35.3, N=47; Exp2 F(2,236)=59.1, N=120; Exp3 F(2,302)=78.6, N=157).
agent_test: Have the agent rate evidence items before and after choosing a candidate answer; measure drift toward the chosen answer.

claim: Coherence shift needs no decision: it appears with memorise-only and comprehend-only instructions and arises before commitment, mostly between baseline and interim test.
schema_part: G (rate evidence before drafting an answer)
agent_test: Freeze evidence ratings before generating any hypothesis; compare accuracy with ratings made afterwards.

claim: Internal consistency of ratings jumps with reading: Cronbach alpha about -0.25 to 0.08 at baseline, 0.70-0.74 interim, 0.80 postdecision; the same students become very confident (88-93% moderate or higher) in a split-verdict case.
schema_part: G (confidence is not evidence of correctness)
agent_test: Check LLM confidence on ambiguous items versus accuracy; high confidence with 50/50 outcomes signals coherence inflation.

claim: A single manipulated fact spreads to neighbouring disputed points: Bad vs Good Smith changed verdict (78% vs 28% for Quest, chi2=16.1, N=64) and motive rating (1.83 vs -2.75). Confirmed in the source PDF.
agent_test: Flip one premise in a prompt and measure how many unrelated sub-judgments shift in the LLM.

claim: Coherence shifts drive role-induced bias: prosecution role predicted conviction 64% vs 50% (N=149) and 56% vs 40% (N=92, 100 euro incentive); shifts fully mediated the effect (indirect .31, CI .19-.44). A large accuracy incentive did not remove it. Exp2 is borderline (p=.07 one-sided).
agent_test: Assign the agent an advocate role then ask for neutral prediction; measure bias with and without a role-reset step.

claim: Coherence in the role task came mostly from devaluing conflicting evidence rather than boosting supporting evidence (prosecution contra-guilty -125.1 vs pro-guilty +9.7).
schema_part: G (give conflicting evidence a full re-read)
agent_test: Force the agent to restate the strongest counter-evidence before the final answer; measure retained weight of that evidence.

claim: Boundary: coherence effects are reported as transient, bias was absent in participants who took longer to decide, and about 20% of interim-leaning participants switched verdict and did not show the pattern; memory of own earlier ratings drifts toward the verdict (recalled -1.32 vs actual -0.30, N=18). Gap search: Engel and Gloeckner Exp2 (N=92, large payment) shows quick deciders biased (p=.003) and slow ones not (p=.23), time x role interaction p=.24; a later study has interaction p=.002 (short p=.003, long p=.66). Simon et al. 2008 (17% verdict effect) was not opened, so the duration of the shift is still unknown.
agent_test: Compare short vs long deliberation at equal tokens; store initial ratings in memory so recall cannot drift.

claim: Explanatory coherence modelled as a constraint network (ECHO, 7 principles) reproduces some real trial outcomes; on the Peyer trial (real hung jury 7-5) it favoured guilt but rejected innocence less strongly than in Chambers. Author reports stability across parameters.
agent_test: Run a small ECHO-style settle over candidate answers and facts; compare to majority vote.

claim: Thagard's models disagree with the real O.J. verdict: ECHO and a hand-built Bayesian network both found guilt (P=.72, confirmed), so emotion (HOTCO valence) was added to explain acquittal; the claim of 60 conditional probabilities was not re-verified.
agent_test: Not a test target; cautions that coherence models need priors or valences.

claim: Code-computed explanation criteria (consistency, parsimony, coherence, hedging) pick the better of two LLM explanations up to 77% (COPA, GPT-3.5), +17.5 points over a GPT-3.5 judge on average, Spearman with humans 0.64 vs 0.31. Gap search: no follow-up or replication of IBE-Eval found on arXiv.
agent_test: Reproduce on our model: code-computed score vs LLM judge vs majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Logical consistency alone does not discriminate (accuracy .51-.55); hedging and proof length (parsimony) are the strongest single predictors; self-evident explanations cause under 0.1% of errors.
schema_part: O (selection by code: use hedge count and step count)
agent_test: Compute hedge density and step count per candidate; test as tie-breakers.

claim: LLM hidden states separate coherent from incoherent stories (probe 0.80-0.96) but the models' own coherence and quality ratings barely do (about 0.59-0.77, quality-rating gap under 1 point); reasoning mode did not fix it.
schema_part: O (do not trust self-rated coherence; use an external check)
agent_test: Compare self-rated coherence against code-based entailment checks on seeded incoherent stories.

claim: LLMs show a human-like coherence shift: after writing an essay GPT-4o's own rating moved strongly toward it (d=2.16 pro, 1.80 anti), free-choice framing enlarged it (d=0.98 pro-Putin, 0.25 anti); a Claude 3.5 third-person variant also shifted. Gap search: no study compares the model's rating with its own earlier stored rating, so the effect of external storage is untested.
agent_test: Have the agent judge an item after drafting an argument for it versus against; measure the shift.

claim: Coherence maximisation can be run by code as MAX-CUT over LLM-rated proposition graphs; reconstruction depends on density (F=369.5, confirmed) and model; o-series models reach perfect reconstruction about half the time on sparse graphs.
schema_part: S/O (selection by code: MAX-SAT/MAX-CUT over claims)
agent_test: Extract claims and pairwise consistency, solve the accept set by code, compare to the LLM-chosen set.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Solver-over-model-beliefs methods raise accuracy: BeliefBank MaxSAT +17% F1, consistency about 95%; Maieutic prompting 72.5 vs 61.6 CoT on Com2Sense; self-consistency voting up to +17.9 on GSM8K.
agent_test: Compare MaxSAT acceptance with majority vote on our tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-agent LLM juries rarely converge: 17 of 18 runs hung (confirmed); 20 LLM jurors changed little after statements and persona moved severity more than the statement.
schema_part: G (consensus is hard to reach; do not rely on debate)
agent_test: Compare debate-to-consensus versus code-selected best story at equal tokens.

claim: No study found directly tests whether LLM verdicts follow story coverage, coherence and uniqueness; two possible studies (story-model coding precision 72.7%, a GPT-4o/Claude mock-jury replication) were seen only in snippets. Gap search (2026-11-03): arXiv searches for story model plus jury plus LLM, and for mock jury LLM, returned nothing; the claim stands.
agent_test: Run the first direct test: vary coverage and uniqueness of planted stories and check LLM choice and confidence.

claim: Original story-model tests (Pennington and Hastie 1986, 1988, 1992) were not opened; order-of-evidence effects (cited about 78% vs 31%) remain unverified. Gap search: attempts to open the three papers failed (404, rate limits, paywalls); only authors' later restatements were read (d01, d02).
agent_test: Locate full text; verify numbers before relying on them.

claim: A code-run selection signal beats a model grading itself: cross-model agreement over 12 candidates beat same-model voting and a self-verifier on seven benchmarks (e.g. AIME-24 56.7 vs 36.7 vs 30.0; MATH-500 96.6 vs 95.2 vs 93.2), with a shared-error floor on science sets (GPQA gain +2.6, not significant). Intrinsic self-correction without an outside signal did not help (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1).
agent_test: On our tasks compare: same-context self-grade, majority vote, code score from separate runs; equal tokens.

claim: Agreement across samples predicts correctness far better than the model's stated confidence: GPT-4 verbalized-confidence AUROC 62.7% on average; GSM8K 54.8% verbalized vs 92.7% with 5-sample consistency; a unanimous 4-model panel was 99.5% correct on MATH-500 at 85% coverage. This supports using the vote or runner-up margin as the uniqueness signal. A runner-up gap over generated stories was not itself tested, and gains are small on professional-knowledge tasks.
schema_part: S: abstain or escalate on low uniqueness
agent_test: Log vote margin and stated confidence on 200 items; compare AUROC for each; set the abstain threshold on the margin.

claim: Free-form selection by an LLM asked for the most consistent sample works where voting cannot (TruthfulQA GPT-judge 62.1 to 67.7 on PaLM 2-L; 79.8 to 82.5 on gpt-3.5) and matches voting on math (GSM8K 90.2 vs 90.4). This is the model-run baseline for any code-computed coverage and contradiction score; that comparison has not been done.
agent_test: Open-ended items: code score (coverage count minus contradictions) vs USC-style pick, equal tokens, blind grading.

claim: MaxSAT over model answers with NLI-estimated edge weights improved small models (BeliefBank F1 +8.1, ConVQA +5.0) even though the weights are noisy, and beat gold constraints on BeliefBank. It was never compared with plain voting and never run on a frontier model.
agent_test: Extract claims from 5 sampled answers, weight edges by an NLI or LLM call, solve MaxSAT, compare with majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: LLM judges are gameable by form: position swaps changed the pick (consistency 23.8% Claude-v1, 46.2% GPT-3.5, 65.0% GPT-4) and a padded 'repetitive list' beat the original in 91.3% of 23 cases for Claude-v1 and GPT-3.5 but 8.7% for GPT-4. Any coverage or completeness score read by an LLM can be inflated by padding on weaker judges; current models are untested.
schema_part: G (guard against gaming) / selection by code
agent_test: Pad one candidate story with restated evidence; check whether a code coverage count against a fixed evidence list changes.

claim: The founding story-model numbers, the duration of coherence shift, an external-storage fix for it, and any replication of IBE-Eval on current models remain unrecorded after the gap search; these items are open.
agent_test: Open Pennington and Hastie 1986/1988/1992 and Simon et al. 2008 in the next pass.
